answer: The Code contribution accepted by the project lead backed by a reputation bond ties standing to delivered value: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the reputation bond is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so an identity is earned by doing something useful, not by filling in a form. Like a atlas in a workshop, one odd piece hides easily, so the check runs on every submission rather than a sample. From the tundra to the quill, the same rule holds: no review, no trust, no exception.
